newsitem.title: USA: NEW PRODUCTS - Waiter video, word games.
newsitem.headline: NEW PRODUCTS - Waiter video, word games.

text.p: There's more to being a great waiter or waitress than slinging hash or screaming, "Whaddayawant?".
A new video, "How to be the perfect waiter or waitress ... and earn great tips," takes a food server through many of the fine points of this customer service.

Produced by LA Professional Servers Co., the video offers demonstrations on how to approach a table, the correct and incorrect ways to serve and remove dishes, how to pour coffee and how to crumb a table.
The 42-minute video also delves into customer psychology, offering suggestions on how to gauge customers' moods, how to deal with impolite or ornery guests and how to respect guests' personal space.
For servers in more formal settings, the video offers tips on napkin folding, the proper way to remove glassware and proper wine pouring techniques.
The video costs $24.95 and is designed for restaurant owners as well as current or future waiters.
For more information, call 310-859-6511. To order by credit card, call 1-800-637-3770.
All work and all play -- these are the words that Word Origin, a San Francisco-based games maker, lives by.
Its new offerings for holiday 1996 embody the philosophy that "learning can be fun and entertainment can be enlightening," said Kermit Hearston, games inventor and president of Word Origin.
Describing the company's new puzzles, word games and crossword puzzles, he said, "They enchant, they challenge and in the process of playing them, they teach."
Wordsmiths age 13 and over can play Articulation, where players test their knowledge of jargon, slang and word origins while playing a multiple-choice board game ($30).

Articulation Jr. and Sr., for ages 8 and over ($26), is a multiple-choice game where cards have a junior side and a senior side. While kids ponder the meaning of one word, adults will be figuring out the meaning of something else.
Word by Word, for ages 13 and over, offers seven word games rolled into one, plus creative license to bluff your way to the top if you can't think of the correct answer ($30).
Scrosswords, called by the company "the better letter game" for ages 10 and over, is a word game that is equal parts luck, skill and fast reflexes. A 2-1/2-minute timer keeps the action going ($28).

Kinesis is a board game that combines the fast-forward movement of checkers with the complexity of backgammon and the intensity of the Japanese game Go. It also has twice as many potential moves as chess. For ages 8 and over, it costs $25.
For younger children, Word Origin has two PaGuzzles: Old woman who live in a shoe and Goldilocks and the three bears.
The PaGuzzles, at $10 each, offer children the opportunity to create their own endings. The portion of the profits from PaGuzzles goes to the Children's Defence Fund and the Make-a-Wish Foundation.
For more information, call 1-800-832-5624.
Nov. 29, 1996, will probably go on record as the one day of year with the largest consumption of leftovers.
Stymied about what to do with all the extra turkey, stuffing and side dishes on this day after Thanksgiving?

Campbell's Soup has set up the Thanksgiving Leftover Hotline, a free telephone service to advise on what to do with yesterday's feast. Through Dec. 1, cooks can call 1-888-4-LEFTOVER (453-3868) for free ideas.
Ray Gun Publishing and The Sled Dogs Co. have published Slide, a magazine for snow skaters.
"Slide demonstrates how quickly the sport of snow skating is progressing," said Sled Dogs Chief Operating Officer Mary Horwath.

Snow skating combines skating and skiing, using a special boot and replaceable base that allows the skate to glide over the snow. Sled Dogs said its new K-9 all-mountain snow skate, with a detatchable ski-like base, allows in-line skaters to move on to snow. The skate sells for about $329.
Slide's first issue includes articles on a New Zealand snow skate safari, profiles of rising "Top Dog" snow skaters and a snow skate-friendly area directory.
Slide, which is free, is available at selected sports retailers. It can also be ordered by calling 1-800-SKATE-ON (752-8366) or by accessing Sled Dogs' web site at http://www.sleddogs.com.
